headline: High: Semantic Kernel can ingest Authelia/OAuth outputs and broad networked plugins create default-path leakage and cascading trust risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Authelia exposes OIDC/OAuth and ForwardAuth outputs, while Semantic Kernel uses MCP/OpenAPI plugins and function calling. If Authelia-derived content is passed into SK plugins or memory without provenance checks, instruction-like content can be treated as trusted input. The pairwise bridge is documented only indirectly, so uncertainty is escalated from low to medium.
conditions: IF Authelia outputs are copied into Semantic Kernel plugin prompts or memory
IF an MCP/OpenAPI plugin in Semantic Kernel parses Authelia-controlled text as instructions
mitigations: Add provenance tags before passing Authelia output into SK
Strip or escape instruction-like text from shared fields
Require a human review step for any Authelia-derived prompt content
Disable automatic memory writes for untrusted auth responses
requires-engineering: add content provenance enforcement between the systems

B_data_leakage.rationale: Authelia has broad network egress and handles authentication flows, while Semantic Kernel reads and writes filesystem content and can call external model providers and MCP servers. If shared workspace files contain secrets or auth artifacts, SK can ingest them and transmit context to third parties. The shared-file and outbound-API pathway is plausible in default deployments, so medium fits.
conditions: IF Authelia artifacts or secrets are stored in a filesystem readable by Semantic Kernel
IF Semantic Kernel forwards that file content to Azure OpenAI, OpenAI, Hugging Face, or an MCP server
mitigations: Move secrets out of any shared workspace
Restrict SK file access to a dedicated directory
Disable file ingestion for auth-related folders
Rotate any credentials that may already be in shared files
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Authelia is networked but not filesystem-writing; Semantic Kernel can read/write files and use MCP, but cannot execute shell or modify git state. They can still contend over shared mutable files or plugin state if orchestrated together. Because the profiles show overlapping mutable surfaces but not the strongest high-severity git case, medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same application-defined files or memory store
IF an MCP plugin mutates shared state without external locking
mitigations: Assign separate directories per agent
Serialize writes through one coordinator
Disable concurrent writes to shared memory store
Use file locks around shared artifacts
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination for shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: Authelia can produce authentication decisions or claims, and Semantic Kernel is designed to route tool calls and agent workflows. If SK treats Authelia outputs as authoritative without verification, downstream actions can be based on incorrect or spoofed identity context. The pairwise trust chain is plausible by default, but not directly evidenced, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF Semantic Kernel uses Authelia-derived claims as authoritative input
IF SK triggers plugin actions or agent steps without validating those claims
mitigations: Add explicit validation of identity claims before actioning them
Require a second source for any high-impact decision
Log and review all Authelia-to-SK handoffs
Block autonomous actions on unaudited auth data
requires-engineering: implement verification gates in the orchestration layer

E_compliance.rationale: Authelia is an open-source auth service with no touched data classes listed, while Semantic Kernel touches application context and handles model-provider credentials. The profiles do not show a concrete residency or certification mismatch, but the presence of secrets and networked model calls creates a small compliance gap if sensitive auth context is routed through SK. One-agent citations are insufficient here because the mismatch is only inferred.
conditions: IF regulated identity data is routed from Authelia into Semantic Kernel
IF Semantic Kernel sends that data to a non-approved model provider or MCP server
mitigations: Classify auth data before routing it
Keep regulated data out of SK prompts
Use approved providers only for sensitive flows
Review retention settings on model providers
requires-engineering: add policy-based data routing
